title: Word order 1
note: Order-first. Check/Type = scramble the given English words. CZ only as a light Use cue. Closed A1 lexis. · classfix B/D/E-2026-07-25 · place order · Bank 26 · intro rewrite 2026-08-05 (first-5 path pass) · sequencing rewrite 2026-08-06 (cloud): bank + intro re-authored on pool-legal lexis only; adj+noun fork closed 2026-08-08 (cloud): 'new' -> 'nice', the only pool-legal adjective at this path position

items.en: I have a car.
accepts: I have a car
items.explanation: Subject → verb → object: I / have / a car. Czech drops 'já'; English needs the subject.
items.explanation_cz: Podmět → sloveso → předmět: I / have / a car. Čeština 'já' vynechá, angličtina ne.

items.en: She has a phone.
accepts: She has a phone
items.explanation: Subject → verb → object: She / has / a phone. Never 'She a phone has'.
items.explanation_cz: Podmět → sloveso → předmět: She / has / a phone. Nikdy 'She a phone has'.

items.en: He needs books.
accepts: He needs books
items.explanation: Subject → verb → object: He / needs / books.
items.explanation_cz: Podmět → sloveso → předmět: He / needs / books.

items.en: We need a teacher.
accepts: We need a teacher
items.explanation: Czech 'Potřebujeme' shows the person in the ending. English shows it with the word We, and We comes first.
items.explanation_cz: České 'Potřebujeme' má osobu v koncovce. Angličtina ji řekne slovem We, a to stojí první.

items.en: They have two dogs.
accepts: They have two dogs
items.explanation: Subject → verb → object. The number goes before the noun: two dogs.
items.explanation_cz: Podmět → sloveso → předmět. Číslo stojí před podstatným jménem: two dogs.

items.en: I have a bag.
accepts: I have a bag
items.explanation: Czech 'Mám' is enough on its own. English needs I in front of the verb.
items.explanation_cz: České 'Mám' stačí samo. Angličtina potřebuje I před slovesem.

items.en: She has three dogs.
accepts: She has three dogs
items.explanation: She / has / three dogs. The number stays before the noun: three dogs.
items.explanation_cz: She / has / three dogs. Číslo zůstává před podstatným jménem: three dogs.

items.en: He is a teacher.
items.cz: On je učitel. (povolání → a/an + job, ne the)
accepts: He is a teacher
He's a teacher
items.explanation: The order does not change with be: subject → verb → rest. He / is / a teacher.
items.explanation_cz: S 'be' se pořadí nemění: podmět → sloveso → zbytek. He / is / a teacher.

items.en: I have English on Monday.
accepts: I have English on Monday
items.explanation: Czech starts with the time. English puts the time at the end: I have English on Monday.
items.explanation_cz: Čeština začíná časem. Angličtina dává čas na konec: I have English on Monday.

items.en: He needs a car on Saturday.
accepts: He needs a car on Saturday
She needs a car on Saturday
items.explanation: Czech puts the time between the subject and the verb. English keeps subject → verb → object together and puts the time last.
items.explanation_cz: Čeština dává čas mezi podmět a sloveso. Angličtina drží podmět → sloveso → předmět pohromadě a čas dá nakonec.

items.en: She has Czech on Friday.
accepts: She has Czech on Friday
He has Czech on Friday
items.explanation: Nothing goes between the subject and the verb: She has … . The time goes at the end.
items.explanation_cz: Mezi podmět a sloveso nic nepatří: She has … . Čas jde na konec.

items.en: We have two students on Wednesday.
accepts: We have two students on Wednesday
items.explanation: Two changes from the Czech: add the subject We, and move the time to the end.
items.explanation_cz: Dvě změny oproti češtině: doplnit podmět We a přesunout čas na konec.

items.en: They have English at two o'clock.
accepts: They have English at two o'clock
They have English at two
items.explanation: Time at the end, after the object: They have English / at two o'clock.
items.explanation_cz: Čas na konci, až za předmětem: They have English / at two o'clock.

items.en: I have a house in Pilsen.
accepts: I have a house in Pilsen
items.explanation: Place goes at the end, after the object: a house in Pilsen.
items.explanation_cz: Místo jde na konec, až za předmět: a house in Plzně.

items.en: She has friends in Cerny Most.
items.cz: Ona má kamarády na Černém Mostě.
accepts: She has friends in Cerny Most
He has friends in Cerny Most
items.explanation: Place last: She has friends / in Cerny Most.
items.explanation_cz: Místo nakonec: She has friends / in Černý Most.

items.en: He has a car in Shanghai.
accepts: He has a car in Shanghai
She has a car in Shanghai
items.explanation: Subject → verb → object, then place: He / has / a car / in Shanghai.
items.explanation_cz: Podmět → sloveso → předmět, pak místo: He / has / a car / in Šanghaj.

items.en: Klara has a phone in the bag.
accepts: Klara has a phone in her bag
Klara has a phone in her bag.
Klara has a phone in the bag.
items.explanation: A name is the subject and stands in the same first position. The place phrase keeps its own order: in the bag.
items.explanation_cz: Jméno je podmět a stojí na stejném prvním místě. Předložková fráze má vlastní pořadí: in the bag.

items.en: I have English in Liberec on Monday.
items.cz: V pondělí mám angličtinu v Liberci.
accepts: I have English in Liberec on Monday
I have English on Monday in Liberec
items.explanation: When both appear, place before time is the normal order: in Liberec on Monday. The Czech here has them the other way round. The other order is not wrong, just less neutral.
items.explanation_cz: Když jsou obě, obvyklé pořadí je místo před časem: in Liberec on Monday. Čeština je tu má obráceně. Druhé pořadí není chyba, jen je méně neutrální.

items.en: She has students in Lysa Nad Labem on Friday.
items.cz: Ona v pátek má studenty v Lysé nad Labem.
accepts: She has students in Lysa Nad Labem on Friday
He has students in Lysa Nad Labem on Friday
She has students on Friday in Lysa Nad Labem
He has students on Friday in Lysa Nad Labem
items.explanation: Place before time is the safer order: in Lysa Nad Labem on Friday. 'on Friday in Lysa Nad Labem' is also heard.
items.explanation_cz: Bezpečnější pořadí je místo před časem: in Lysé nad Labem on Friday. 'on Friday in Lysé nad Labem' se také říká.

items.en: He has Czech in Pardubice on Tuesday.
items.cz: On v úterý má češtinu v Pardubicích.
accepts: He has Czech in Pardubice on Tuesday
She has Czech in Pardubice on Tuesday
He has Czech on Tuesday in Pardubice
She has Czech on Tuesday in Pardubice
items.explanation: Place first, then time: in Pardubice on Tuesday. Both go after the object.
items.explanation_cz: Nejdřív místo, pak čas: in Pardubice on Tuesday. Obojí jde za předmět.

items.en: We have English in Warsaw at three o'clock.
items.cz: Ve tři máme angličtinu ve Varšavě.
accepts: We have English in Warsaw at three o'clock
We have English in Warsaw at three
We have English at three o'clock in Warsaw
We have English at three in Warsaw
items.explanation: Add the subject We. Place before time is the normal order: in Warsaw at three o'clock. At three without o'clock is fine too.
items.explanation_cz: Doplňte podmět We. Obvyklé pořadí je místo před časem: in Varšava at three o'clock. At three bez o'clock je také správně.

items.en: I need a nice phone.
accepts: I need a nice phone
items.explanation: The adjective goes before the noun: a nice phone. The article stays first: a / nice / phone.
items.explanation_cz: Přídavné jméno stojí před podstatným: a nice phone. Člen zůstává první: a / nice / phone.

items.en: She has a nice car.
accepts: She has a nice car
items.explanation: a + adjective + noun: a nice car. Never 'a car nice'.
items.explanation_cz: a + přídavné jméno + podstatné jméno: a nice car. Nikdy 'a car nice'.

items.en: He needs a nice bag.
accepts: He needs a nice bag
items.explanation: Order inside the object: a / nice / bag. Never 'a bag nice'.
items.explanation_cz: Pořadí uvnitř předmětu: a / nice / bag. Nikdy 'a bag nice'.

items.en: I meet friends in Dolni Pocernice.
items.cz: Potkávám se s kamarády v Dolních Počernicích.
accepts: I meet friends in Dolni Pocernice
items.explanation: Add the subject I. Czech 'se' has no English word here: I meet friends. Place goes last.
items.explanation_cz: Doplňte podmět I. České 'se' tu nemá anglické slovo: I meet friends. Místo jde nakonec.

items.en: She has a bag in the car.
accepts: She has a bag in the car
He has a bag in the car
items.explanation: Place at the end: She has a bag / in the car.
items.explanation_cz: Místo na konci: She has a bag / in the car.

cards.title: What it is
points: S = who · V = action · O = what / who
Keep this order in simple positive sentences
English likes a clear order: **Subject → Verb → Object** (SVO).

cards.title: Place and time
points: Place and time usually go **at the end**.
If both appear, put **place before time**.
The other order is not wrong — it is just less neutral.

cards.title: Common mistakes

rows: Always she has English on Monday.

points: CZ tip: don't put the object before the verb
Place before time is the safer order when both are at the end

rows: on Saturday / a car / he needs
